title: Reliability activation field kit for product launch (90-day plan)
summary: Practical, minimal-friction playbook for feature/product teams to onboard SLOs, validate operational readiness, and run the first 90 days of reliability experiments leading up to GA. Focused on lightweight artifacts, role checklists, and a sprintable backlog so product launches don't fall into ‘reliability debt’.
body:
Purpose
-----
This is a field kit: a compact, cross-functional operational plan to bring a new product or major feature to a reliable, observable state over 90 days. Goal is to move teams from no-SLOs -> pragmatic SLOs + basic guardrails + automated alerting and canary cadence. This is intentionally opinionated and minimal: avoid long docs, create working artifacts.

When to use this
- New public feature launch with >1k expected daily active users or significant revenue/latency sensitivity
- Major model-serving rollout (new model family, new quantization profile, or significant architecture change)
- Platform teams handing off a service to feature owners for production responsibility

Core outcomes (Success criteria)
- 1–3 pragmatic SLOs defined and accepted by feature owners (latency/availability/error budget).
- Basic dashboards covering latency p50/p95, error rate, and request volume for the feature route.
- Alerts with clear escalation paths and playbooks for top 3 failure modes.
- Canary + rapid rollback policy validated in at least two staged deployments.
- Weekly reliability review loop with product and engineering for the first 90 days.

Roles & responsibilities (one-liners)
- Feature owner (Product lead) — sets business impact thresholds, participates in SLO tradeoffs.
- Service owner (Backend eng lead) — implements metrics, SLOs, and runbook hooks.
- eng-sre (on-call + reliability eng) — helps define error budgets, configures alerting, assists canary tooling and incident runbooks.
- Observability owner (Console/monitoring eng) — builds the minimal dashboard and ensures traces/logs are surfaced.
- Solutions engineering / SE (optional for customers) — runs customer-facing validation and capacity checks.

Quick checklist (Day 0 -> Day 7)
1) Day 0: Kickoff (30–60m)
   - Participants: Product, Service owner, eng-sre, Observability owner.
   - Deliverable: 1-page charter (link to this doc) + primary contact names.
2) Day 1–3: Instrumentation sweep
   - Ensure latency and error metrics exist for feature route(s).
   - Tag traces with feature_id / route metadata.
3) Day 3–5: Draft SLOs
   - Propose a single availability SLO (e.g., 99.5% successful responses for route X) and a latency SLO (p95 < 350ms for critical path).
   - Compute raw error budget burn for current week (baseline). Document in the charter.
4) Day 6–7: Minimal dashboard + alerts
   - Dashboard with p50/p95 latency, error rate, traffic, and request-rate.
   - Pager/Slack alert for sustained error-rate > threshold for 5m or p95 latency > threshold for 3m.

90-day sprint map (high-level milestones)
- Sprint 0 (week 0): Kickoff, instrumentation, SLO draft, baseline measurement.
- Sprint 1 (weeks 1–2): Alert refinement, first canary run, basic runbooks for top-3 incidents.
- Sprint 2 (weeks 3–4): Alarmless automation: automated rollback triggers for canary, runbook rehearsals.
- Sprint 3 (weeks 5–7): Load and failure-mode inject tests, capacity knobs review (batching, qprofiles).
- Sprint 4 (weeks 8–10): Customer-impact drills, error-budget policy, oncall handover plan.
- Sprint 5 (weeks 11–12): GA readiness review, documentation handoff, retrospective and continuous improvement backlog.

Weekly ritual template
- Reliability check-in (30m)
  - Who: feature owner, service owner, eng-sre, observability owner
  - Agenda: SLO burn update, notable alerts/incidents, canary status, unresolved action items
  - Output: updated action tracker and owner assignment

Tactical backlog (pick from this list during sprints)
- Create feature-scoped metrics tags (feature_id, route_version)
- Add synthetic canary trace with warmup traffic
- Implement prefix/KV caching validation for latency-sensitive endpoints
- Create an automated rollback job triggered by canary fail-state
- Add end-to-end smoke test in CI that exercises the observability path
- Run a 30-minute chaos experiment for the top 2 dependencies (DB, model store)
- Define and store runbook snippets under /runbooks/<feature> for top 3 incidents

Acceptance criteria (for sign-off at GA)
- SLOs defined and documented with owner + review notes.
- Dashboards linked in the feature’s README and Console route page.
- Alerting saturation test passed (simulate 2x traffic, validate no alert storm escalation path).
- Canary policy validated and documented: duration, traffic split, rollback thresholds.
- On-call rota includes at least one person who understands the feature; handover notes created.

Operational runbooks (short examples)
- Symptom: sudden p95 latency spike for route X
  - Immediate: Check canary status and recent deploys. Run pinned smoke test.
  - If canary failed and deploy happened in last 30m: rollback to previous version, notify product.
  - If no deploy and dependency error seen: open incident, escalate to dependency team.
- Symptom: sustained error budget burn > 30% in 24h
  - Freeze non-critical releases, switch to reduced QPS mode (rate-limit nonessential paths).
  - Trigger emergency reliability review with Product and Eng-SRE.

Dependencies & escalation path (practical notes)
- Observability: ensure ingestion filters don't drop low-volume but high-signal traces.
- Platform: reserved GPU pool access for canary scale testing must be granted by day 10.
- Security/Compliance: any telemetry including PII must be validated by security before dashboards go public.

Known risks & mitigations
- Risk: teams treat SLOs as checkbox -> mitigation: require SLO tradeoff doc signed by Product.
- Risk: alert fatigue -> mitigation: use error-budget based rate limiting and actionable thresholds.
- Risk: hidden perf regressions post-quantization -> mitigation: add regression tests that compare token latency distributions pre/post quantization.

Lightweight artifacts to produce (and share)
- One-page SLO tradeoff note (business impact, proposed SLOs, risk tolerance)
- Dashboard snapshot (PNG) + URL
- Canary run report (short, includes timestamps, traffic split, outcome)
- Top-3 incident runbook snippets in /runbooks/<feature>

Unresolved questions (items to decide in week 0)
- Which metric should be primary for the feature: request-success rate or model-output-quality proxy?
- What is the acceptable burn threshold that triggers release freezes? 25% or 30% of error budget/day?
- Who will own the postmortem if the incident is caused by a downstream dependency?

Notes to self / working assumptions
- Keep SLOs tight enough to reflect customer experience but loose enough to avoid continual release blocks.
- Encourage feature teams to run small fault injections rather than wait for production incidents.
- This kit assumes minimal observability plumbing exists; if not, escalate to platform team for a 2-week instrument sprint.

Next steps (for the kickoff owner)
- Circulate this field kit to stakeholders and book the 30–60m kickoff within 2 business days.
- Create the SLO tradeoff note in the linked confluence page and tag eng-sre for review.
- Assign dashboard and canary owners in the first reliability check-in.

History & changelog
- 2026-01-14: Draft created by Maya Patel
- 2026-02-03: Added tactical backlog and runbook snippets (Ethan Ross)
- 2026-02-24: Incorporated canary rollback automation notes and sprint cadence (Diane Wu)

Appendix: quick command checks (for engineers)
- Check current p95 latency (example): curl -s "https://metrics-api/featureX/p95" | jq
- Trigger synthetic canary (example): ./scripts/trigger_canary.sh --feature X --duration 10m

-- END OF FIELD KIT --
